A 16 years- old male was involved in a quarrel. He was admitted to hospital with headache and vomiting. On examination, he was confused with scalp injury in the right tempro-parietal region. Few hours later, he passed into coma with unequal pupil size and the heart rate was 55 beats/minute.
a) What is your diagnosis? What is the proper management of such case?

A 19 year-old female was found dead in a clinic. On examination, her body was pale and a small fetus (16 cm in length) was found beside her body, the length of the uterus was 6 inches. The obstetrician claimed that this was a case of therapeutic abortion and has been complicated to death.
a. How could you estimate the age of the victim?
b. Does the fetus belong to the victim? Why?
c. What are the possible causes of death in this case?
d. What are the investigations requested by the medical examiner for this case?
e. Are there any medicolegal responsibilities on the obstetrician? Why?

A 20 year-old woman brings her 7 years old son into the emergency department for a broken arm. The child has been to the emergency department twice before for various injuries. The mother lives with her husband who is not the child's father. The mother simply states that the child is accident prone. When you ask her whether her husband may be injuring the child she becomes very angry and vigorously denies it.
a. What should you do?

A 21 year-old male who was detained in custody for a minor offence, alleged maltreatment and physical harassment by the police. On examination, there were multiple linear bruises on his back, together with rounded deep seated burnt areas on the chest and circular bruises around the wrists.

b. Try to guess the causative agents of the detected injuries?
c. How could you estimate the age of these bruises?
d. Do the detected injuries support or nullify the allegation? Justify your answer.

A 21 year-old man was found dead in his bathroom, lying on his left side. There was blood beneath his head, associated with a laceration to the posterior scalp together with multiple linear contusions allover the body. On exam. his body shows patchy hypostasis and rigor mortis of the face & neck. Autopsy showed large wedge shaped intra-cerebral hemorrhage tapered deep into the brain substance. Some red stain was found on the bed sheet and bathroom. Serology investigations revealed that the blood stain from the bathroom belongs to the deceased, while the stain on the bed was not blood.

A 21 years old male who was detained in custody for a minor offence, alleged maltreatment and physical harassment by the police. Careful examination revealed that the area of the bottom of the buttocks was spared. But characteristic old circular scars with a tail were found on the back of the child. A 35-year-old single female was found on her bed stuporous after attempting suicide by ingesting different pills including barbiturates. The family immediately called the ambulance and she was taken to a nearby hospital. The physician began to insert a nasogastric tube to aspirate the contents of the stomach. As he was, attempting to get the tube down, the patient became briefly more responsive and cried out that she did not want the tube, she did not want any treatment and that she wanted to be left alone and allowed to die. She moaned that she had left a note, which said she wanted to die and she meant it. The family arrived in the next few minutes and urged that the doctor continued treatment. The physician realized that if she had consumed the pills in the bottles she will not have survived without medical treatment and yet it seemed clear that she did not want any treatment.

options.b: Does the principle of patient autonomy apply here?
options.c: Can the physician perform a treatment against the consent of the patient?

question:
iv. M.L.I. of lucid interval:
a. Medical responsibility of negligence:
Any victim after head's trauma must be kept under medical observation (24- 48 hours) for signs of cerebral compression for surgical decompression in the proper time. Physician must observe all vital functions of the victim, pupils, consciousness state and motor power every 15 minutes.
Decompression operation is done to remove bone or hematoma, if pulse rate becomes less than 60 beats / minutes.
If the pt is discharged before 48 hours and dies from the compression, the treating practitioner is legally responsible.
b. The assailant may deny the responsibility: because the victim has regained his normal life.
c. The victim may tell about the assailant and whole circumstances.
b. i. Ethics of gene therapy: Gene therapy is simply the introduction of a specific functioning gene into cells for therapeutic or preventive purposes.
1) The con-elation of defective gene should be restricted to serious diseases.
2) It must be used only when there is no alternative available.
3) Experience with animal studies must be sufficient to assure effectiveness of the techniques used.
4) A written consent should be provided by the patient after discussing the risks and disadvantages of the procedures to the patient.
ii. Rapid causes of death from burns → within the first 48 hours: 6-48 hours:
1) Hypovolemia and hemoconcentration: due to loss of plasma from the burnt area and vasodilatation caused by the release of histamine like substance.
2) Edema of the glottis and pulmonary edema: especially in burns of the neck and due to irritation by the inhaled hot gases and irritant fumes.
3) Fat embolism: especially in burns of fatty areas.
4) Toxemia and his famine shock: destroyed tissues → release of toxins especially histamine → massive capillary dilatation and hypovolemic shock.
5) Infection (36-72 hours), as local sepsis, septicemia. Inflammation of serous membranes as peritonitis. Also bronchopneumonia may be a cause.
